newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices to rise 10% in 1997 - UBS.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices to rise 10% in 1997 - UBS.

text.p: British house prices are set to rise by 10 percent over the course of next year and a further 10 percent in 1998, UBS said on Tuesday.
If the UBS report is proved right, 1997 will be the first year to boast double-digit house price increases since 1989.
Turnover would also increase sharply as negative equity melts away, reaching 1.4 million transactions next year and 1.6 million in 1998, the UBS survey said.
Between the end of 1995 and the end of the year 2000, house prices will rise by a cumulative 46 percent, UBS forecast.
"With housing seriously undervalued by any historical comparison the market's new-found confidence will fuel a rapid catching up period," said Rob Thomas, analyst at UBS.
He said there was only a small danger of a speculative boom as long as the UK economy did not seriously overheat.
He also said the idea that the housing market performed best in periods of high inflation could be proved wrong.
"If low inflation is accompanied by low interest rates, the burden of debt servicing costs will be light, making housing affordable," Thomas said.
